# Test fixtures

## APNG synthetic fixtures

All files in `apng/` are original, deterministic AniView test data generated by
`tools/apng/generate-fixtures.mjs`, using Node's zlib PNG compression and explicit
PNG CRCs. There is no copied artwork or third-party binary content. Fixture data
may be reused under CC0-1.0. Regenerate with Node 24:

```sh
node tools/apng/generate-fixtures.mjs
```

The encoded images follow the [W3C PNG/APNG specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/png-3/).
Most canvases are 3×2 pixels, enabling exact full-frame RGBA assertions in the
real-worker browser check. `expectations.json` records manually specified canvas
results and container metadata, independently of the application compositor.
Alpha-blended colors may differ by one channel unit after browser premultiplication.

| File | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `full-infinite.png` | Default PNG image included as frame 0; two full frames; 20/40ms; infinite loop |
| `full-finite.png` | Two full frames; two total plays |
| `composition.png` | Partial rectangles, offsets, transparent SOURCE, alpha OVER, NONE, BACKGROUND and PREVIOUS |
| `hidden-default.png` | Magenta default PNG image excluded; animation begins on transparent canvas with partial frames |
| `first-previous.png` | First-frame PREVIOUS must behave as BACKGROUND |
| `delays.png` | Zero duration, zero denominator (100), 1ms duration and one total play |
| `static.png` | Ordinary PNG, no `acTL` |
| `long-bounded.png` | 100 frames, 64×64, 100ms, infinite loop; cache-bound observation |

Parser tests also mutate chunk lengths, CRCs, frame counts, rectangles, sequence
numbers and operations. These corrupt variants are generated in test memory,
keeping repository fixtures small.

## External desktop samples (downloaded, ignored)

The real-world integration sample `.tools/fixtures/bouncing-beach-ball.png` is
Holger Will's public-domain [bouncing beach ball](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Animated_PNG_example_bouncing_beach_ball.png):
63,435 bytes, 100×100, 20 frames, 75ms/frame, infinite loop. Downloaded through
the [apngasm-python sample mirror](https://api.github.com/repos/laggykiller/apngasm-python/contents/samples/input/ball.apng),
whose upstream documentation credits Wikimedia Commons. Git blob:
`1b35084a369ee5d40908a70e01ca47fccb144ce4`.
SHA-256: `ce0905f339f44370c0fecc226ef4b422d86f06a3ec4f194e5cfb9d0b50aafb2e`.

An additional [Web Platform Tests sample](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/images/apng.png)
is downloaded as `.tools/fixtures/wpt-apng.png`: 259 bytes, 100×50, two 11ms
frames, one total play. It is subject to the WPT BSD 3-clause license.
SHA-256: `76c3568f8dbf0adcdf15d8a42acd96815ccf317d566118d569c218725167d0a0`.

Neither downloaded binary is committed. These real external samples supplement
the committed synthetic conformance fixtures rather than replacing their pixel
assertions. Measured desktop results are not Android performance claims.
